product_family: Zotero is a free, open-source research tool for collecting, organizing, and analyzing bibliographic data. Includes desktop app, web interface, and optional cloud sync via AWS. Available with optional library synchronization to Zotero servers or WebDAV.

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type 1
certifications.proof_quote: No mention of SOC 2 on Zotero's own security page. In a Zotero Forums thread, a Zotero team member wrote: "These are enterprise certifications that aren't realistic for an organization of our size."

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type 2
certifications.proof_quote: No mention of SOC 2 Type 2 on Zotero's own security page or elsewhere in public Zotero documentation; no formal attestation reports have been published.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No mention of ISO 27001 on Zotero's own security page. In the same Zotero Forums thread, the team characterized formal certifications like this as 'enterprise certifications that aren't realistic for an organization of our size,' pointing to open-source auditability as an alternative.

certifications.name: GDPR Compliance
certifications.proof_quote: Zotero privacy policy states 'All Zotero server data is stored in the United States in Amazon Web Services.' No GDPR annexes, Data Processing Agreement, or GDPR compliance statement found in public documentation. US-based servers raise concerns under post-Schrems II judgment.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of HIPAA compliance or Business Associate Agreement. Security documentation notes data encrypted at rest with AES-256, but Zotero/AWS staff have access to decrypted data. Not marketed as HIPAA-compliant.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of PCI DSS certification. Credit card processing handled by third party, but no specific certification mentioned.

certifications.name: HECVAT (Higher Education Community Vendor Assessment)
certifications.proof_quote: "We can provide a HECVAT (an assessment tool used by higher-education institutions to evaluate security and privacy) on request." (Zotero team, Zotero Forums). Separately, some institutions report friction completing the broader compliance review despite this offer.

privacy.ai_training_note: Terms of Service contain no mention of AI training, machine learning, or model development using user data. However, no explicit opt-out or commitments were found either.
privacy.data_region: United States (AWS us-east-1 region). Privacy policy explicitly states 'All Zotero server data is stored in the United States in Amazon Web Services.' Raises GDPR concerns for EU users post-Schrems II judgment.

security.name: Encryption in Transit
security.value: Yes, using current best practices. SSL Labs rates Zotero API endpoint with A+ score.

security.name: Encryption at Rest
security.value: Yes, AES-256 for newly created accounts. Synced data stored on AWS.

security.name: Open Source
security.value: All software is open source and available for auditing. Code-signed builds for macOS and Windows.

security.name: Default Data Storage
security.value: Local-first design. All research data remains local by default unless user explicitly enables syncing.

security.name: Synced Data Access
security.value: Access limited to essential Zotero staff when syncing enabled. Data stored in AWS us-east-1.

security.name: Server Logs Retention
security.value: Server logs retained for 90 days maximum.

security.name: Backup Retention
security.value: Automated backups may be retained for up to 6 months.

security.name: Formal Security Audit
security.value: No evidence of external formal security audits or penetration testing reports.

products.name: Zotero Desktop
products.data_scope: Local storage by default. Optional cloud sync via Zotero servers or WebDAV.
products.notes: Free, open-source application. No account required for local use. Runs on Windows, macOS, Linux.

products.name: Zotero Web
products.data_scope: Requires synced Zotero account. Data stored on US-based AWS servers.
products.notes: Requires user to enable sync on desktop app. Access to library from any browser.

products.name: Zotero Cloud Storage
products.data_scope: Optional add-on. Syncs research libraries to AWS us-east-1.
products.notes: Available as optional paid add-on or free limited tier. Encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit.

compare.pricing_model: Free open-source desktop app with optional paid cloud storage tiers (File storage; GB packages available)
compare.data_residency: US-based (AWS us-east-1). Users can self-host via WebDAV or keep data local only.

flags: Zotero lacks SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and all standard enterprise compliance certifications. The organization is transparent about this limitation.
US-based servers (AWS) without a formal DPA raise compliance concerns for GDPR-regulated organizations after the Schrems II ECJ judgment.
No Data Processing Agreement was found in public documentation, despite Zotero being used in education and healthcare.
Some universities have removed Zotero from computers due to its refusal or inability to complete HECVAT or other formal compliance documentation.
The Corporation for Digital Scholarship emphasizes open-source and privacy-first design as an alternative to formal certifications, rather than pursuing SOC 2 or ISO 27001.
There is no public information about whether a DPA, HECVAT completion, or other enterprise compliance support is available upon request.
The terms contain no AI training clause, but also no explicit commitment against AI training on user data.
Any AWS certifications (SOC 2) belong to Amazon, not Zotero; Zotero does not hold these directly.
